items.passage: The sea still stretched emptily before him; the dotting sails still unchanged and distant. Yet a strange shadow lay upon the raft. He turned his head with difficulty. On the opposite side--so close upon him as to be almost over his head--the great white sails of a schooner hovered above him like the wings of some enormous sea bird. Then a heavy boom swung across the raft, so low that it would have swept him away had he been in an upright position; the sides of the vessel grazed the raft and she fell slowly off. A terrible fear of abandonment took possession of him; he tried to speak, but could not.
items.question: In the text, the schooner's great white sails most likely represent?
options: a danger the man escapes only by lying flat
the distant sails he had watched all along
a sign that death has already claimed him
a chance of rescue that nears and passes
items.explanation: 배는 그를 거의 덮칠 만큼 가까이 왔지만 결국 천천히 멀어진다. 곧이어 '버림받는 공포'가 그를 사로잡는다는 문장에서, 돛은 다가왔다가 사라지는 구조의 가능성을 상징함을 알 수 있다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 붐을 피한 것이 의도된 행동이 아니므로, B는 멀리 있던 돛과 이 배가 구별되므로, C는 지문에 죽음이 이미 왔다는 근거가 없으므로 틀리다.

items.passage: The white mists were still curtseying to one another across wider spaces in the valley, and the dim light behind them grew slowly stronger. There was a scent of turf-smoke on the air from a fire which someone had lit under a bank a little way down the hill. The very strokes of old Dan Heron’s hammer continued to come up in a faint rap-tap from the roadside, where he was breaking lumps of reddish sandstone; for Dan was so deaf that he applied himself to his tasks with abstracted concentration, and could not easily be interrupted. Evidently the news had not penetrated to him. A murmur of voices was passing to and fro in a knot of men gathered at a short distance. Pierce might have caught a sentence now and then.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “curtseying to one another” most nearly suggests that the mists are?
options: moving gently as if bowing to each other
clearing away suddenly before the sunrise
hiding the men gathered down the hill
thickening as the turf-smoke spreads
items.explanation: 'curtseying'은 무릎을 굽혀 인사하는 동작으로, 안개가 골짜기에서 서로를 향해 부드럽게 움직이는 모습을 의인화한다. 이어지는 문장에서 빛이 '천천히' 강해진다는 묘사도 느리고 고요한 아침 분위기를 뒷받침한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 '갑자기' 걷힌다는 점, C와 D는 사람을 숨기거나 연기로 짙어진다는 근거가 없다는 점에서 틀리다.

items.passage: I chronicle wild doings in this place, and have no time for the sweets of love long denied. But strange as the bridal had been, so the nuptials were strange, one like the other played to a steel undertone. When Richard had his Jehane, at first he could not enjoy her. He rode away with her like a storm; the way was long, the pace furious. Not a word had passed between them, at least not a reasoned word. Once or twice at first he leaned forward over her shoulder and set his cheek to her glowing cheek.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “played to a steel undertone” most nearly suggests that the marriage had?
options: a cheerful music that filled the wedding feast
an underlying harshness running beneath it
a display of wealth in the couple's armor
a quiet sadness felt only by the narrator
items.explanation: 'steel undertone'은 결혼 밑에 깔린 차갑고 거친 기운을 음악 비유로 표현한 것이다. 리처드가 신부를 '폭풍처럼' 데려가고 속도가 '맹렬했으며' 제대로 된 말 한마디 없었다는 묘사가 이를 뒷받침한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 즐거운 음악, C의 부의 과시, D의 화자만의 슬픔은 지문 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
I brought my doom upon myself,
And there I was upon the shelf
In melancholy.
Why, say you, did I go at all?
I once met Chloris at a ball,
And in my folly
I went and suffered all this pain
In hopes to see her once again.

Of strawberries a pound at least
I ate, and made myself a beast
With tea and sherry;
And raspberries I ate and trembled,
Until I felt that I resembled
Myself a berry,
But 'twas the berry that at school
We used to call a gooseberry fool.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “upon the shelf” most nearly suggests that the speaker was?
options: proudly displayed for everyone to admire him
busily serving food to the other guests
set aside and ignored by those around him
safely hidden from the woman he loved
items.explanation: 'upon the shelf'는 선반 위에 올려진 물건처럼 쓰이지 않고 밀려나 있는 상태를 뜻한다. 바로 뒤의 'In melancholy'와 스스로 '파멸'을 불렀다는 첫 줄이 화자가 무도회에서 소외되어 우울했음을 보여 준다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 감탄의 대상이라는 점, B는 음식을 대접했다는 점, D는 클로리스를 다시 보려고 갔다는 내용과 맞지 않아 틀리다.

items.passage:
On one hand we see an enormous increase in the brain power of the people--a multitude able to think, eager to think, not to be prevented from thinking, where only two or three generations ago the thinking was done exclusively by the few. On the other hand we see the necessity for more thinking, for vigorous stirring-up of the minds of the masses, for more and more education. And, year by year, the stirring-up process increases. The evils of the present day are as old as the race, as old as ignorance, as old as human frailty. The good, the benefits, are new, entirely new.

The material and mental forces of modern civilization have already wrought wonders.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “vigorous stirring-up of the minds of the masses” most nearly suggests a need for?
options: a violent disturbance that threatens order
a blending of all classes into one group
a confusion that stops people from thinking
an energetic effort to awaken thinking
items.explanation: 'stirring-up'은 휘저어 깨우는 동작으로, 대중의 정신을 활발히 일깨우는 일을 비유한다. 같은 문장에서 이것이 '더 많은 사고'와 '더 많은 교육'의 필요와 나란히 제시되고, 앞 문장도 생각하려는 대중의 증가를 말한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 폭력적 혼란, B의 계층 혼합, C의 사고 마비는 교육을 긍정하는 글의 흐름과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: The mystical element in him was for ever reaching out in search of some Divine essence in the world. He was not in search at any time of personal relations. He attracted more affection than he ever gave; he rejoiced its sympathy and kindred companionship as a flower rejoices in sunshine; but I think he had little taste of the baffled suffering which accompanies all deep human passion. He once wrote "God has preserved me extraordinarily from intimacies with others. He has done this, not I. I have longed for intimacies and failed to win them." He had little of the pastoral spirit; I do not think that he yearned over unshepherded souls, or primarily desired to seek and save the lost. On the other hand he responded eagerly to any claim made to himself for help and guidance, and he was always eager not to chill or disappoint people who seemed to need him.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “as a flower rejoices in sunshine” most nearly suggests that the man felt?
options: a natural, easy pleasure in others' warmth
a constant struggle to earn people's affection
a fragile need that withered without company
a strong urge to seek out lonely, lost souls
items.explanation: 꽃이 햇빛을 즐기듯이라는 직유는 그가 타인의 공감을 애쓰지 않고 자연스럽게 즐겼음을 뜻한다. 같은 문장에서 그는 '준 것보다 많은 애정을 받았고' 깊은 열정의 고통은 거의 몰랐다고 하여 이를 뒷받침한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 애정을 얻으려 애썼다는 점, C는 그가 개인적 관계를 찾지 않았다는 점, D는 길 잃은 영혼을 찾지 않았다는 서술과 어긋난다.

items.passage: Positively such a thing had become possible. She, who had never ______ her impulses before, had gradually learned to control them for this simple girl’s sake. On the one or two occasions, early in their acquaintance, when she had let her evil spirit get the better of her, the sudden pain and wonder in Georgie’s face had stung her so quickly, that she had resolved to hide her iniquities, at least in her presence. Sometimes she had even wished that she had been softer at heart and less selfish. It was so unpleasant to see herself just as she was, when she breathed that sweet atmosphere of which I have spoken.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: expressed
restrained
overlooked
enjoyed
items.explanation: 빈칸 뒤에서 그녀가 이 소녀를 위해 충동을 '통제하는 법을 점차 배웠다'고 하므로, 이전에는 충동을 억누른 적이 없었다는 대조가 필요하다. 이어 자신의 악한 면을 숨기기로 결심했다는 문장도 이를 뒷받침한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A, C, D는 '배웠다'와의 대조를 만들지 못해 논리적이지 않다.

items.passage:
The electric light had not been turned on. The window was open, the curtains were drawn back, and a little light came from the moon, not long risen.

For a moment Mrs. Hawkes saw nothing. Then, her eyes becoming accustomed to the gloom, she perceived that there was something on the floor close by the window, something that did not move, did not utter a sound.

She moved forward quickly, and knelt down on the floor. Then a shudder went through her, and she sat back with a low cry.

Once more bending down, she raised the ______ mass from the floor, turned the limp head, stared down into the ghastly face.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: eager
restless
inert
graceful
items.explanation: 앞에서 창가의 무언가가 '움직이지도, 소리를 내지도 않는다'고 했고, 빈칸 뒤에서도 머리가 '축 늘어져' 있다고 한다. 따라서 움직임이 없는 상태를 뜻하는 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 활동적인 상태를, D는 우아한 움직임을 뜻하므로 문맥과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Some one has said of the Scotch novels, that that is the best which we happen to have perused last. It is thus that I estimate the relative value and virtue of the Months. The one which happens to be present with me is sure to be that one which I happen to like better than any of the others. I lately insisted on the ______ of January on various accounts. Now I have a similar claim to put in in favour of the next in succession. And it shall go hard but I will prove, to the entire satisfaction of all whom it may concern, that each in her turn is, beyond comparison, the “wisest, virtuousest, discreetest, best.” Indeed I doubt whether, on consideration, any one (but a Scotch philosopher) will be inclined to dispute the truth of this, even as a logical proposition, much less as a sentiment.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: plainness
brevity
dullness
supremacy
items.explanation: 화자는 지금 함께 있는 달을 '다른 어떤 달보다 더 좋아하게 된다'고 말한다. 다음 달에 대해서도 '비슷한 주장'을 하겠다고 하므로, 1월이 가장 뛰어나다고 주장했다는 의미가 필요하다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A, B, C는 칭찬이 아니라 단점을 가리키므로 흐름과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Health means soundness of body and of mind; the keeping of our physical system in such a condition that it is able to do its work easily, without disturbance, and without pain; the exercise of the mind so as not to harm the body. There are certain preliminary considerations that we should bear in mind in connection with this subject.

I. The ______ connection between body and mind.--They are both related to each other in some mysterious way. So close is the connection that the one cannot be affected without the other. The well-being of the one depends on the well-being of the other. The power which the mind has over the body and the body over the mind has been well and tersely described by a writer of our time.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: close
distant
recent
simple
items.explanation: 빈칸 뒤에서 한쪽이 영향을 받으면 다른 쪽도 반드시 영향을 받는다고 하고, 한쪽의 안녕이 다른 쪽에 달려 있다고 말한다. 이는 몸과 마음의 연결이 매우 밀접함을 뜻하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 정반대 의미이고, C와 D는 연결의 강도를 설명하지 못한다.

items.passage:
The hills were very stony, and so light was the soil upon them, that the rain rendered the ground very soft. The river had many fine reaches, extending in straight lines from one to three miles, and of a corresponding breadth. The rapids, although ______, offered no material obstruction to the boats. The current in the long reaches was scarcely perceptible, and it appears to me that the difference of elevation between this station and the last is not considerable.

June 8.--The river expanded into beautiful reaches, having great depth of water, and from two to three hundred feet broad, literally covered with water-fowl of different kinds: the richest flats bordered the river, apparently more extensive on the south side.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: absent
frequent
gentle
invisible
items.explanation: 'although'는 앞뒤 내용의 양보 관계를 나타내므로, 급류가 배에 방해가 되지 않았다는 점과 대조되는 성질이 필요하다. 급류가 '자주' 있었지만 방해가 되지 않았다는 의미가 자연스러우므로 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 존재하지 않으면 양보가 성립하지 않고, C는 방해가 없다는 내용과 대조되지 않아 틀리다.

items.passage: The description of the forest was a description of the wood where she had first met Harcourt; the charm of it returned, until she almost seemed to again inhale its balsamic freshness in the pages before her. Now, as then, her youth came back with the same longing and regret. But more bewildering than all, it was herself that moved there, painted with the loving hand of the narrator. For the first time she experienced the delicious flattery of seeing herself as only a lover could see her. The smallest detail of her costume was suggested with an accuracy that pleasantly thrilled her feminine sense.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: It moves from wistful remembrance to pleased surprise at her portrayal.
It moves from amused detachment to bitter anger at the narrator.
It moves from fearful suspicion to calm acceptance of Harcourt's absence.
It moves from careful analysis to boredom with the book's details.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 그녀는 하코트를 처음 만난 숲을 떠올리며 '그리움과 후회'를 느낀다. 그러나 'But more bewildering than all' 이후 자신이 연인의 눈으로 그려졌음을 깨닫고 '달콤한 아첨'과 즐거운 전율을 느낀다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 분노, C의 의심, D의 지루함은 지문에 나타나지 않는다.

items.passage:
Miss Field won the first and third, her antagonist contenting himself with the second. It had always been so, and for ten years she had taken a childish delight in her skill. "My dear Doctor," she often said, "it takes a woman of brains to play chess."

"It does, indeed," he invariably answered, with an air of gallantry. Once he had been indiscreet and had won all three games, but that was in the beginning and it had never happened since.

When the clock struck ten, he looked at his heavy, old-fashioned silver watch with apparent surprise. "I had no idea it was so late," he said.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From bitter rivalry to warm reconciliation between the two players.
From Miss Field's pride to gentle irony about the Doctor's losses.
From cheerful conversation to sudden alarm at the lateness of the hour.
From solemn reflection to open mockery of Miss Field's chess skill.
items.explanation: 처음에는 필드 양이 체스 실력을 '어린아이처럼' 기뻐하는 모습이 그려진다. 그러나 박사가 한 번 '경솔하게' 세 판을 다 이긴 뒤 다시는 그런 일이 없었다는 서술에서 그가 일부러 져 준다는 은근한 아이러니가 드러난다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 원한, C의 놀람, D의 공개적 조롱은 근거가 없다.

items.passage: The drainage has been rendered better, and the fearful odours that met you at every turn have disappeared. The poor are indolent, dirty, thriftless, and ill-housed; but that does not much matter, as most of their lives are passed in the open air. The convents are suppressed, the schoolmaster is abroad, and they may grow better as the years roll by, and Italy, as a nation, once more becomes great and renowned. But a good deal has yet to be done. I heard of things to be seen in Naples of the most disgraceful and disgusting character.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From harsh condemnation to full satisfaction with Naples' progress.
From playful humor to deep grief over the suffering of the city's poor.
From measured hope about reforms to sharp disapproval of what remains.
From detached description to warm praise for Italy's former glory.
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 배수 개선, 학교 교육 등을 들며 이탈리아가 '나아질 수도 있다'고 조심스럽게 기대한다. 그러나 'But a good deal has yet to be done' 이후 '수치스럽고 역겨운' 일들을 언급하며 비판적 어조로 바뀐다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 순서가 반대이고, B의 슬픔과 D의 과거 찬양은 지문 근거가 없다.

items.passage: The high-priced quartet has never been relied upon, the chorus choir being preferred, not merely for its own singing, but because it served best in leading the congregation, and that was the thing ever kept in mind. Mr. Beecher loved the old-fashioned hymns, though he had also a hearty welcome for new ones, and he was never satisfied unless he got everybody to singing. I have often seen him jump up from his chair right in the middle of a hymn and hold up his hand for silence. "You are not singing this hymn right," he would say. "Sing it with more spirit, and let everybody sing."
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From fond praise of Beecher to sharp criticism of his strict methods.
From excitement about new hymns to regret over losing the old ones.
From formal complaint about the choir to amused approval of the quartet.
From calm explanation to a lively scene of Beecher in action.
items.explanation: 앞부분은 비싼 사중창단 대신 합창단을 둔 이유를 차분히 설명한다. 이후 'I have often seen him jump up' 부분부터 비처가 찬송 도중 벌떡 일어나 손을 들고 직접 외치는 생생한 장면으로 바뀐다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 비판, B의 후회, C의 사중창단 칭찬은 지문 내용과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
The loss of her son struck the final blow to Mrs. Hale's already declining health, and a severe attack of fever, which for some time threatened her life, left her totally blind. She arose from her bed of sickness, a sadder but a wiser woman, confessing the folly and weakness of which she had been guilty in her treatment of Tom.

She was no longer able to work for herself, and her friends advised her to go into the workhouse. But the poor woman clung so fondly to her old home, every corner of which was familiar to her, and into every room of which she could soon grope her way by means of a stick, that Sir Herbert, to whom the cottage belonged, consented to her staying in it as long as she liked.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a misfortune that blinds Mrs. Hale and how she keeps her home.
It recounts Tom's return home and then describes Mrs. Hale's joyful recovery.
It compares the cottage with the workhouse and then argues for the workhouse.
It introduces Sir Herbert as a landlord and then lists the rules of his cottages.
items.explanation: 첫 단락은 아들을 잃은 충격과 열병으로 헤일 부인이 시력을 잃는 불행을 서술한다. 둘째 단락은 일할 수 없게 된 그녀가 구빈원 대신 익숙한 집에 계속 머물게 되는 과정을 보여 준다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 톰의 귀환이 없고, C는 구빈원을 옹호하지 않으며, D는 허버트 경이 잠깐 언급될 뿐이라 틀리다.

items.passage:
Tam would have come into it almost intact. He might have been able to educate himself while he was yet young, to spare himself many a drudging day and weary night.

But looking back calmly over the gulf of years, with the mountains of difficulty well past, the man decided it was better as it had been. He had profited by the warfare he had undergone--it had made twice the man of him that he might have been otherwise. It was more honourable to have hewed out the fortune which he honestly thought so great and enviable, than to have derived even a part of it from the gift of another.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It lists Tam's many hardships and then blames another person for them.
It imagines an easier past for Tam and then why he prefers his own.
It describes Tam's present fortune and then predicts how he will spend it.
It recounts a quarrel over a gift and then describes how it was settled.
items.explanation: 첫 단락은 탐이 재산을 물려받았다면 일찍 교육받고 고생을 덜 했을 것이라는 가정을 제시한다. 둘째 단락은 'But' 이후 그가 지난 투쟁이 자신을 두 배의 사람으로 만들었으므로 실제 삶이 더 나았다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 남 탓, C의 미래 예측, D의 다툼은 지문에 없다.

items.passage:
Be sure that every motive which comes not from the single eye; every motive which springs from self; is by its very essence unheroic, let it look as gaudy or as beneficent as it may.

But I cannot go so far as to say the same of the love of approbation--the desire for the love and respect of our fellow-men.

That must not be excluded from the list of heroic motives. I know that it is, or may be proved to be, by victorious analysis, an emotion common to us and the lower animals. And yet no man excludes it less than that true hero, St. Paul.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It praises St. Paul's heroism and then lists the motives he rejected.
It defines heroism and then argues that no human motive is heroic.
It rejects selfish motives and then defends one, love of approval.
It describes animal emotions and then contrasts them with human habits.
items.explanation: 글은 먼저 자기에게서 나온 동기는 본질적으로 영웅적이지 않다고 단언한다. 이어 'But' 이후 인정받고 싶은 욕구만은 예외라고 하며 반론을 인정한 뒤 성 바울을 예로 들어 옹호한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 성 바울이 마지막 예시일 뿐이고, B는 예외를 인정하는 내용과 어긋나며, D는 동물 감정이 반론의 일부로만 언급되어 틀리다.

items.passage:
Miss Terry passed her hands over her eyes and glanced at the clock. But what the hour was she never noticed, for her gaze was filled with something else. Beside the clock, in the spot where she had laid it a few minutes before, was the Christmas Angel. __But now, instead of lying helplessly on its back, it was standing on rosy feet, with arms outstretched toward her.__ Over its head fluttered gauzy wings. From under the yellow hair which rippled over the shoulders two blue eyes beamed kindly upon her, and the mouth widened into the sweetest smile.

"Peace on earth to men of good-will!" cried the Angel, and the tone of his speech was music, yet quite natural and thrilling.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why Miss Terry failed to notice the hour on the clock.
It describes the Angel as it looked when Miss Terry first bought it.
It suggests that Miss Terry has accidentally knocked the Angel over.
It marks the moment when the lifeless figure seems to come alive.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 등을 대고 '힘없이' 누워 있던 인형이 이제 장밋빛 발로 서서 팔을 뻗고 있다고 대조한다. 이후 날개가 펄럭이고 눈이 빛나며 천사가 말을 하는 장면으로 이어지므로, 이 문장은 인형이 살아나는 전환점이다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 앞 문장의 결과일 뿐이고, B와 C는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
For the campaign was now approaching its climax.

The public man is always two wholly different personalities. There is the man the public sees--and fancies it knows. There is the man known only to his intimates, known imperfectly to them, perhaps an unknown quantity even to himself until the necessity for decisive action reveals him to himself and to those in a position to see what he really did. __Unfortunately, it is not the man the public sees but the hidden man who is elected to the office.__ Nothing could be falser than the old saw that sooner or later a man stands revealed.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It states a troubling result of the claim that public men have two selves.
It gives a historical example of a political candidate who was at last revealed.
It agrees with the old saying that a man eventually stands revealed.
It shifts the focus from public figures to the narrator's own campaign.
items.explanation: 앞 문장들은 공인에게 대중이 보는 사람과 숨겨진 사람이라는 두 인격이 있다고 설명한다. 밑줄 문장은 'Unfortunately'와 함께 선출되는 쪽은 숨겨진 사람이라는 문제적 결과를 제시한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 구체적 사례가 없고, C는 마지막 문장이 그 격언을 부정하며, D는 화자의 선거운동이 언급되지 않아 틀리다.
